note: Board overview. Each board's full profile lives in <id>.json in this folder, using the same fields as the Blue Pill pin table. price is a rough USD range at typical US retailers (Amazon, Adafruit, SparkFun, DigiKey), for budgeting only

boards.name: Freenove ESP32-WROVER (with camera)
boards.why: The board in this kit. USB-C flashing, WiFi/BLE/camera

boards.name: Blue Pill STM32F103C8T6
boards.why: For the lowest budget and for people who want to learn a real STM32 directly; it has the most gotchas (clone chips, serial needs an extra adapter), so it suits learners with a platform or a mentor to lean on

boards.name: Nucleo-F103RB (official ST board)
boards.why: For people who want to learn STM32 without wasting time on flashing and serial: it has a built-in programmer and USB serial, works the moment you plug it in, and the chip is in the same family as the Blue Pill

boards.name: Nucleo-F411RE (official ST board)
boards.why: For people who want a faster chip, far more Flash/RAM and a hardware FPU, for displays, audio and control-algorithm projects

boards.name: ESP32 DevKit board
boards.why: For people who want Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and small IoT gadgets; strong performance at a low price, but the pins are not 5V-tolerant and the boot pins are fussy

boards.name: Arduino UNO R3
boards.why: For complete beginners: the most tutorials, and 5V peripherals connect directly; but it has the weakest performance and memory, so you will outgrow it eventually
